construction_markdown:
Use the composite-level Drinfeld modular curve over F_256 from the proof, but replace its 16,512 zero coordinates by a two-level deterministic distance-repair block.

The original main subcode B_0 has dimension 3,915,352 and distance at least D=469,762,048. Enlarging its one-point divisor by 91 gives a nested code B_91 with 728 additional binary dimensions and distance at least D-5,824. Enlarging once more and retaining two binary directions gives B_92 with two further dimensions and distance at least D-5,888.

For the first repair layer, use the Hermitian curve Y^8 Z+Y Z^8=X^9 over F_64. A deterministically selected degree-149 place gives an outer [513,122,>=364]_64 AG code. Concatenation with RM(1,5)=[32,6,16]_2 gives [16,416,732,>=5,824]_2; retain a deterministic 730-dimensional subcode. Map B_92/B_0 isomorphically into this code.

For the second layer, map B_92/B_91 into the explicit [96,2,64]_2 code (u,v) -> (u^32,v^32,(u+v)^32). The graph of these two quotient maps has exact length 1,073,725,312+16,416+96=2^30 and dimension dim(B_92)=3,916,082.
distance_audit: The main base code B_0 has distance at least 64(8,388,479-1,048,447)=469,762,048.
Every nonzero word of B_91 has weight at least 64(8,388,479-1,048,538)=469,756,224=D-5,824.
Every nonzero word of B_92 has weight at least 64(8,388,479-1,048,539)=469,756,160=D-5,888.
The Hermitian auxiliary code has distance at least 364*16=5,824; taking a 730-dimensional subcode preserves this bound.
The repeated-simplex code [96,2,64] supplies the additional 64 units needed by the top two-dimensional quotient.

For b in B_0, the main block alone contributes D. For b in B_91 minus B_0, the main and Hermitian blocks contribute (D-5,824)+5,824. For b in B_92 minus B_91, all three blocks contribute (D-5,888)+5,824+64. These cases cover every nonzero codeword.
explicitness_audit: The main base ring, reduction prime, three powered level primes, residue fields, modular curve, divisor degrees, and coordinate orderings are explicitly fixed.

The canonical composite-level Drinfeld modular curve is symbolically recoverable through the cyclic modular polynomial, projective closure, normalization, and good reduction, with reduced Gröbner bases and lexicographic tie-breaking at every algebraic step.
The nested main spaces are selected by deterministic enumeration and greedy exact linear independence; the final two directions are explicitly the F_2-span of h and alpha*h.
F_64 is F_2[zeta]/(zeta^6+zeta+1), with its polynomial basis and coefficient ordering fixed.

The degree-149 Hermitian place is the lexicographically first Frobenius orbit of size 149 in a lexicographically specified degree-149 extension of F_64. Hasse-Weil proves that this enumeration terminates.

Both Reed-Muller encoders use truth tables ordered by binary integers. The Hermitian basis, its 730-dimensional subcode, both quotient maps, the repeated-simplex coordinates, and the final block order are deterministic.
There is no random sampling, probabilistic existence argument, puncturing, unspecified shortening, or hidden asymptotic constant.

obstructions: An uncoupled direct sum would have minimum distance equal to the minimum constituent distance. The quotient-dependent graph construction is essential for adding the two repair weights to the appropriate main-code losses.

A single-level enlargement by 92 full F_256 directions would require 736 auxiliary dimensions at distance 5,888; the Hermitian constituent does not certify that. The nested 728+2 split is what makes the final two dimensions rigorous.
Official publication remains blocked until two separate verifier agents record acceptances, even though no mathematical step in this submission is conditional.

proof_markdown:
### Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with parameters

[1,073,741,824, 3,916,082, >=469,762,048]_2.

Its rate is 1,958,041/536,870,912, strictly greater than 7/1920.

### 1. The modular-curve base

Put A=F_2[T], with the pole of T as infinity. Define

rho=T^4+T+1,
p_1=T,
p_4=T^4+T^3+1,
p_8=T^8+T^4+T^3+T+1,

and n=p_1^4 p_4^2 p_8. The two quartics have no binary root and have nonzero remainder modulo the unique irreducible quadratic T^2+T+1, so they are irreducible. For p_8, repeated squaring gives T^256 congruent to T and

T^16+T congruent to T^6+T^4+T^3+T^2 modulo p_8.

The Euclidean remainder chain ends with 1, so Rabin's criterion proves p_8 irreducible. Thus rho is coprime to n.

Let alpha be the residue class of T modulo rho. The trace of alpha^3 from F_16 to F_2 is

alpha^3+alpha^6+alpha^12+alpha^24=1.

Consequently X^2+X+alpha^3 is irreducible over F_16. Fix

K=F_16[beta]/(beta^2+beta+alpha^3)=F_256

with ordered binary basis

(1,alpha,alpha^2,alpha^3,beta,alpha beta,alpha^2 beta,alpha^3 beta).

Let X be the canonical smooth projective good reduction at rho of the rank-two Drinfeld modular curve X_0(n), followed by extension of constants to K. This is a symbolic definition. A coordinate model is recovered deterministically from the cyclic modular polynomial of [Breuer–Rück](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4086), projective closure, normalization, and good reduction; use reduced Gröbner bases and lexicographic tie-breaking throughout.

For this level,

epsilon(n)=24*272*257=1,677,696,
kappa(n)=6*17*2=204.

The rational base field has L-polynomial 1 and class number one. The genus formula of [Bassa–Beelen–Nguyen](https://doi.org/10.1112/S146115701500025X) therefore gives

g=1+epsilon/3-kappa=559,029.

The exceptional term vanishes because p_1 has odd degree. Their rational-point theorem, with reduction degree four and class-group order e=1, gives over K

N_1(X)>=epsilon*(2^4-1)/(2^2-1)=5 epsilon=8,388,480.

The same source gives absolute irreducibility and good reduction in this polynomial-ring, degree-one-infinity setting.

Recover the projective model as above, normalize each projective coordinate tuple at its first nonzero coordinate, order K by its displayed binary basis, and order tuples lexicographically. Let Q_0,...,Q_8,388,479 be the first 8,388,480 rational points. Put L=8,388,479 and evaluate at Q_1,...,Q_L.

Set a_0=1,048,447 and G_0=a_0 Q_0. Riemann-Roch gives

ell(G_0)>=a_0+1-g=489,419.

Enumerate reduced rational expressions in the fixed function-field generators by degree and then lexicographically. Greedily retain the first 489,419 independent elements of L(G_0); call their K-span V_0. Exact function-field arithmetic decides membership and independence, and Riemann-Roch proves termination.

Now put

a_91=a_0+91=1,048,538,
a_92=a_0+92=1,048,539.

Since

ell(a_91 Q_0)>=489,510,

extend V_0 deterministically to a K-linear space V_91 of dimension 489,510 inside L(a_91 Q_0). Also

ell(a_92 Q_0)>=489,511.

Let h be the first enumerated element of L(a_92 Q_0) outside V_91, and define the F_2-linear space

V_92=V_91 direct-sum span_F2{h,alpha h}.

The two displayed classes are independent modulo V_91: if (u+v alpha)h lies in V_91 for u,v in F_2 and u+v alpha is nonzero, K-linearity of V_91 would imply h lies in V_91. Hence dim_F2(V_92/V_91)=2.

Encode every K-symbol by the truth table of the corresponding affine Boolean function in seven variables. This is RM(1,7)=[128,8,64]_2. Let B_0, B_91, and B_92 be the binary evaluations of V_0, V_91, and V_92 after this encoder. Evaluation is injective because every divisor degree is less than L. Therefore

dim B_0=8*489,419=3,915,352,
dim(B_91/B_0)=8*91=728,
dim(B_92/B_91)=2.

A nonzero function in L(aQ_0) has at most a rational evaluation zeros. Hence

d(B_0)>=64(L-a_0)=469,762,048,
d(B_91)>=64(L-a_91)=469,756,224,
d(B_92)>=64(L-a_92)=469,756,160.

### 2. The 16,416-coordinate Hermitian repair

Let E=F_2[zeta]/(zeta^6+zeta+1)=F_64, ordered by the polynomial basis. Rabin's test gives zeta^64=zeta and gcd(Z^6+Z+1,Z^4+Z)=gcd(Z^6+Z+1,Z^8+Z)=1, so the defining polynomial is irreducible.

Over E consider

H: Y^8 Z+Y Z^8=X^9.

Its partial derivatives are X^8, Z^8, and Y^8, so H is a smooth plane curve of degree nine and genus 28. Affinely, y^8+y is the trace E -> F_8: it maps onto F_8 with kernel of size eight. Also x^9 is the norm E -> F_8. Thus every x in E admits exactly eight values of y, giving 512 affine points; there is one point at infinity. Hence H(E) has exactly 513 points.

A degree-149 place exists deterministically. Indeed, 149 is prime and Hasse-Weil gives

#H(F_{64^149}) >= 64^149+1-56*8^149 > 513=#H(E).

Every point over F_{64^149} not defined over E consequently has Frobenius orbit exactly 149. Define F_{64^149} using the lexicographically first monic irreducible polynomial of degree 149 over E, enumerate normalized projective H-points lexicographically, and let Q be the first orbit of size 149. This fixes Q without randomness.

Because deg Q=149>2g-2=54,

ell(Q)=149+1-28=122.

Evaluate L(Q) at all 513 rational points. Its support is disjoint from Q, evaluation is injective, and every nonzero word has at least 513-149=364 nonzero symbols. This gives an exact [513,122,>=364]_64 code.

Encode E by RM(1,5)=[32,6,16]_2 using the polynomial basis and truth-table order. The resulting binary code has parameters

[16,416,732,>=5,824]_2.

Order an E-basis of L(Q) by the same deterministic greedy convention, expand it in the displayed binary basis, and retain the first 730 binary basis vectors. Their span S has exact parameters [16,416,730,>=5,824]_2.

### 3. Multilevel weight-propagation lemma

Lemma. Let B_0 be contained in B_1 contained in B_2 be binary linear codes with respective distance lower bounds D, D-delta_1, and D-delta_2. Suppose A has dimension dim(B_2/B_0) and distance at least delta_1, while R has dimension dim(B_2/B_1) and distance at least delta_2-delta_1. Fix an isomorphism phi:B_2/B_0 -> A and an isomorphism psi:B_2/B_1 -> R. Then

C={(b,phi(b+B_0),psi(b+B_1)): b in B_2}

has dimension dim B_2 and distance at least D.

Proof. The first component makes the parametrization injective. For nonzero b there are three cases. If b lies in B_0, both auxiliary components vanish and the first has weight at least D. If b lies in B_1 but not B_0, phi is nonzero, so the weight is at least (D-delta_1)+delta_1. If b does not lie in B_1, both quotient images are nonzero, giving at least (D-delta_2)+delta_1+(delta_2-delta_1)=D. This also proves the assertion for every nonzero codeword, not merely generators.

### 4. Assembly

Apply the lemma with

B_1=B_91,
B_2=B_92,
delta_1=5,824,
delta_2=5,888,
A=S.

For R use

R={(u repeated 32 times, v repeated 32 times, (u+v) repeated 32 times):u,v in F_2}.

Its three nonzero words all have weight 64, so R=[96,2,64]_2. Order a basis of B_92/B_0 by first listing the 728 directions from V_91/V_0 and then h,alpha h. Map this basis to the ordered 730-vector basis of S. The last two quotient coordinates give the map to R. Thus both quotient maps are completely fixed.

The resulting graph code has length

128*8,388,479+16,416+96
=1,073,725,312+16,416+96
=1,073,741,824=2^30,

and dimension

3,915,352+728+2=3,916,082.

The lemma proves minimum distance at least 469,762,048. All constituent encoders, evaluations, quotient maps, and direct products are F_2-linear, so the final code is binary linear.

### 5. Ceiling comparison

The exact rate is

R=3,916,082/2^30=1,958,041/536,870,912
 =0.00364713557064533233642578125.

Moreover,

R-7/1920=10,487/8,053,063,680>0,

because 15*3,916,082-7*2^23=20,974. The escape from the vanilla GS-RM envelope is genuine: the main curve is the alternative composite-level Drinfeld modular family with an exact cusp correction, and the additional 730 dimensions are obtained by multilevel quotient-coupled distance repair rather than parameter tuning inside the one-level GS formula.
